If I ever have my own company I think I would do all I can to establish 6 hour workdays for all employees instead of 8.

Why? I think that humans are simply unable to work effectively for periods of 8 hours.

At least 2 hours in an 8 hour workday is spent on non work related things like browsing thr web or chatting with coworkers.

8 hour workdays is a 100 year old idea. Why should we blindly accept it and not explore other options?

I think that people work best when they are relaxed and happy, at least in the IT industry but I am pretty sure this also applies everywhere else.

I will add sources to bold claims I made above when I get to my desktop pc.

What do you think? Is 8 hours too much? Is 6 too little? Thoughts?

Simply put, I think we (especially in the U.S.) work way too hard. Back in the 70's we worked 9-5. Now, 8-5 is the norm. I work 9 hour days (in trade for an extra day off every other week). I know that in the E.U. folks generally get a LOT more holidays than they do in the U.S. We were told growing up that new technologies would allow us to work less, however, new technologies have simply drastically increased the productivity demanded by the employer.

I believe that you are a good human with realistic views on making the world a better place.

Personally, the number of hours in the workday wouldn't matter as much to me as the quality of those spent work hours. If the employees are willing and able to do their job with passion and great effort, they wouldn't mind even going overtime voluntarily.

The bigger problem I see here is the way the supervisors engage with their subordinates in the office.

I think that individual employees should be empowered to work as little or as much as they want.

Right now we have a norm of 8 hour work days. If you want a job, you're agreeing to an 8 hour work day. In most places, you can't just work more and get more money. Employers won't allow this, due to overtime obligations. In most (salaried) places, you can't just work less and get less money; I'm less sure of why this is, but this is.

I would like to live in a world where I go to hire someone, and they tell me how many hours they want to work, and I scale their pay appropriately. Mandating a 6 hour workday instead of an 8 hour one doesn't fix any problems, it just trades one set for another. The people who want to work 4 hour days will be slightly happier, and the people who want to work 10 hour days will be slightly more upset.

As an aside: I also work in software, and I completely agree than "eight hour work days" aren't more than 3-4 hours of actual productivity. I think, though, that this is less to do with the raw amount of time and more to do with demoralizing management. I can get eight productive hours in a day on my own projects just fine; it's when other people give me bullshit work is when I get bogged down.

As another aside, consider the following: at least in software, software engineers are provably worth seven figures of revenue to companies, yet even the most well-compensated developers aren't making more than $200k total comp in California. By this measurement, engineers are underpaid (I know that's a shocking thought to the non-engineers here; read this for some hard numbers). Perhaps it's valuable to look at "8 hour workday => 3 productive hours" less as a human capacity thing and more as a "wellp if I'm underpaid so much, I'll underperform". I don't know, I'm not an economist. Just food for thought
